Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Apex Global Asset Management Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. As a reminder, during the question and answer session, to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. Please be advised that today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Global Asset Management's Q3 2024 results. Joining me on today's call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rivera, Chief Financial Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Investment Officer; and David Chen, Head of Distribution.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that some of the statements made today may be forward-looking. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us. I'm pleased to report on our performance for Q3. We achieved solid results this quarter, driven by robust organic expansion, strong net inflows, and strategic acquisitions that bolstered our capabilities in sustainable investing and emerging markets alternatives. Our AUM grew to $1.27 trillion.

Michael Rivera: Thank you, Johnathan. From a financial perspective, Apex Global Asset Management delivered strong results in Q3. Our revenue was $3.5 billion, representing an 18% increase year-over-year. This growth was primarily driven by higher average AUM, resilient fee rates, and elevated performance fees from realizations in our private markets platforms. Our expenses were $2.2 billion, resulting in net income of $850 million. We continue to manage our expenses prudently, with adjusted operating margins expanding meaningfully, as I'll detail shortly.

As of quarter-end September 30, 2024, our total AUM reached a record $1.27 trillion, reflecting a robust 16% year-over-year increase from $1.09 trillion in Q3 2023, and a sequential 4% rise from Q2. This outpaced the industry average, where top global managers saw around 12% growth per Morningstar Direct. Breaking it down, organic growth contributed 6% year-over-year, powered by $65 billion in net inflows—our highest quarterly figure since late 2021. Market appreciation added 9%, riding the S&P 500's strong rally and equity tailwinds from AI optimism and easing inflation. FX translation provided a 1% boost, mainly from a firmer euro; on a constant currency basis, growth was 15%. Average AUM for the quarter hit $1.25 trillion, up 15% year-over-year, supporting a 12% jump in management fees to $2.3 billion.

Geographically, this underscores our diversification strategy amid regional variances. North America, at 55% of total AUM or $687 billion, grew 19% year-over-year, with $42 billion in net inflows. Retail demand flooded our low-cost ETFs, like the Apex S&P 500 ESG ETF, which drew $15 billion—matching Vanguard's top trackers in volume. Institutions added a $10 billion pension mandate into multi-asset credit ahead of Fed cuts. Europe, 24% or $300 billion, rose 13%, with $18 billion inflows into UCITS offerings like the Apex Eurozone Green Bond Fund, attracting €5 billion from defined contribution plans under SFDR. Asia-Pacific, 15% or $188 billion, surged 28% on $12 billion inflows—Japan's GPIF and pensions poured ¥1.5 trillion into yen-hedged ETFs amid Nikkei gains, while China family offices committed RMB 20 billion to private credit. Rest of World, 6% or $75 billion, grew 11%, highlighted by a $3 billion PIF infrastructure commitment tied to Vision 2030.

Turning to organic growth and market share, which highlight our franchise strength and wallet capture in a competitive field. We posted organic AUM growth of 9.2% year-over-year, excluding market moves and inorganic flows—a 11th straight quarter of double-digit expansion on a trailing four-quarter view, beating the industry's 5.8% per Morningstar. Quarter-over-quarter, it was 2.4%, propelled by $14.7 billion net inflows, with outflows at just 1.2% of starting AUM, reflecting our loyal client base.

By asset class, equities led at 12.5%, with $4.2 billion into the AlphaCore Equity Fund amid AI and tech momentum, grabbing 15 basis points of large-cap growth share—like BlackRock's iShares or Invesco's QQQ peers. Fixed income grew 7.8% organically via short-duration and ESG credit, gaining 22 bps in intermediate bonds per Lipper. Alternatives shone at 15.3%, with $6.1 billion into private credit evergreens; our Apex Private Markets at $28 billion expanded pension share by 8%, echoing Ares and Apollo models.

Client-wise, institutions (65% of AUM) hit 10.1% growth on $9.8 billion from SWFs and endowments shifting to alts. Retail/wealth grew 7.9% with $4.9 billion into SMAs; RIA custody ties rose 14% via Envestnet integration. Regionally, U.S. (52% AUM) did 11.4%, adding 18 bps ETF share to 2.7% per ETFGI, on megatrends like semis and renewables. Europe grew 8.7% with €3.2 billion inflows under SFDR, capturing 12 bps from Vanguard in Nordics green bonds. Asia-Pacific accelerated to 14.2%, adding A$2.1 billion via Singapore hubs with DBS/UOB, targeting 2.5% share by 2026 on China stabilization and India capex.

Market share-wise, we're top-10 per Willis Towers Watson, gaining 37 bps institutional wallet YTD per eVestment—4.1% in private credit behind only Blackstone/KKR. Retail ETFs hit 2.4% U.S. share via launches like Apex Semiconductor Innovation ETF (APIX) at $1.8 billion in six months, topping Fidelity/Schwab rivals. Tech like our AI portfolio engine across 70% strategies boosted alpha by 120 bps risk-adjusted, retention to 98.5%; direct indexing at $45 billion competes with Parametric/iShares; portal upgrades lifted advisor adoption 28%, cross-sell to 2.7 products/client.

High-conviction themes: private markets scaling with $50 billion dry powder for 12-15% IRRs in infra/secondaries; sustainable alpha on $210 billion ESG AUM up 18% organically vs. MSCI's 14%, via Article 8/9; next-gen distribution with fintech embeds like Wealthfront/Robinhood. FY24 organic guide: 8-10%, with $35 billion RFP pipeline at 65% conversion; fees compressed just 2 bps on alt mix shift.

Net flows totaled $18.7 billion for Q3, up 22% YoY—strongest since Q4 2021—with YTD at $52.4 billion for 4.2% organic AUM growth to $1.27 trillion, cementing top-five status. Fund performance drove this: active equities (28% AUM) got $9.2 billion on U.S. Large-Cap Growth Fund's 14.2% return, +420 bps over S&P net fees, 11 quarters outperforming, pulling $4.1 billion institutional. Fixed income: Core Bond at 5.8%, +110 bps Bloomberg, drew $3.8 billion retail; alts $3.4 billion on 9.1% private credit IRR. 65% flows to top-two quartiles per Morningstar.

Market trends amplified: equities rally (S&P +8.7%, MSCI World +7.2%) sent $12.5 billion to equity/multi-asset (67% total). ESG at $6.8 billion, Climate Transition ETF +250 bps over iShares peers. Fixed income shift on steepening curve: $4.5 billion to duration, offset $2.1 billion cash outflows. EM mixed: $1.3 billion to India/LatAm on 6.8% GDP, Mexico nearshoring; underweight China.

U.S. flows $11.4 billion (61%), from 401(k)s and wirehouses like Morgan Stanley/Merrill ($1B+ each). Europe $4.2 billion (+48% YoY) on UCITS/Article 8/9. APAC $2.3 billion (+65%) via Hong Kong/Singapore ETFs. Institutions $7.9 billion including $2.5 billion Middle East SWF infra; retail $10.8 billion (+19%) on Apex Digital robo with 150k accounts.

Initiatives: three new ETFs—Semiconductor Innovators ($900M), Green Bond Ladder ($650M), Active EM ($400M)—15% of flows; ETF AUM $320 billion +28% YoY vs. industry 12%. Alpha Engine upped forecasts 15%; direct indexing to $50 billion for 120 bps tax-alpha. Alts to 25% AUM by 2026, $10 billion closings; overweight HY/EM debt for cuts.

Operating margins adjusted to 37.2%, +210 bps YoY from 35.1%, +80 bps sequential; TTM 36.5%, top peer tier like T. Rowe, above 32% industry per Greenwich. Revenue leverage: avg AUM $1.25T +14%, 8% organic $28 billion high-margin alts/ESG, 6% markets; mgmt fees +12% at 52 bps resilient vs. Vanguard/BlackRock passive. Perf fees +25% to $150M on PE carry, hedge 9% > HFRI.

Expenses +7% to $2.8 billion < revenue; comp/benefits +5% on flat headcount 4,200, variable pay on 12% EPS. G&A via zero-based budgeting. Wealth mgmt (45% rev) margins 42% +300 bps on alt cross-sell 85 bps fees vs. 45 bps equities. Institutional 33% slight dip on FI perf fees, offset OCIO +20% to $250B. North America 40%+ on retirement; Europe 35% MiFID resilient; APAC 28% +400 bps on Singapore/China mandates, Alipay/WeChat efficiency -15% acquisition costs.

Tech: AI Alpha cut research 18%; AWS cloud -22% IT; private assets to 25% AUM by 2026 (from 15%), 2-3x fees per McKinsey $10T wave. Q4 margins 37-39%; 80% adj op income to buybacks/2.8% dividend.

On M&A, a key inorganic pillar amid industry consolidation—$50 billion deals YTD per PwC, +15%. Closed two accretive: $450M Verdant Capital ($12B AUM, London ESG UCITS), +85 bps fees, $28M ann rev, 70% integrated to Aladdin, $15M synergies (25% cost rev improve). EMEA inflows $4.2B YTD, cross-sold ESG ETF $120M flows. Second, $320M Pacific Rim Alternatives ($8.5B APAC private debt/real assets), to $45B platform on infra boom (Indonesia JETP, Vietnam RE). 8.5x EBITDA, 60 bps fees; 15% G&A savings on APX Digital AI/blockchain.

Megatrends: alts $20T dry powder McKinsey; ETF active share +20% U.S.; digital. Criteria: 10%+ ROIC 18 mos, 20%+ AUM CAGR, culture. Pipeline $3-5B, five LOIs (U.S. multi-family, fintech APIs, India quant); 1-2 more FY24 for 5-7% AUM ex-markets, M&A 40%. Track record 150 bps EPS acc last five; risks integration/HSR.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Michael. On the investment front, we continue to focus on delivering strong risk-adjusted returns for our clients. Our key strategies performed well, particularly in equities and alternatives. We're navigating the current market environment by emphasizing AI-enhanced alpha generation and ESG integration across portfolios, which has improved outperformance and client retention. We launched the Apex AI Innovators ETF this quarter, and the early reception has been positive, with $900 million in AUM already, capturing thematic flows in semiconductors and beyond.

David Chen: Thank you, Elena. From a distribution perspective, we saw strong inflows into our ETF and alternatives funds. Our efforts to expand our reach in Asia-Pacific are paying off, as evidenced by $2.3 billion in regional net flows, partnerships with local platforms like DBS and UOB, and growth in our Singapore hub driving retail demand.

Johnathan Hale: In summary, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering value to our shareholders. We are focused on executing our strategic priorities and capitalizing on the opportunities ahead. This includes scaling private markets, advancing sustainable alpha through Article 8/9 products, and leveraging next-gen distribution with fintech embeds, all while maintaining expense discipline and pursuing disciplined M&A.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Mike Larson with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Larson: Good morning. Can you provide more details on the organic growth rate and how you're gaining market share in alternatives?

Michael Rivera: Thanks, Mike. As I noted, organic growth was 9.2% year-over-year, outpacing industry at 5.8%, with alternatives at 15.3%—$6.1 billion inflows into private credit. We're gaining 37 bps institutional share YTD, 4.1% in private credit, via our Apex platform's co-investment model, much like Ares. Tech like AI portfolio tools and direct indexing are key, boosting retention to 98.5% and cross-sells.

Mike Larson: Thank you. And a follow-up on operating margin trends—any risks to sustaining 37%+?

Michael Rivera: Great question. Margins hit 37.2% on revenue leverage and 7% opex growth. Asia margins up to 28% on efficient distribution; AI and cloud cuts are structural. Guide 37-39% Q4, with alts mix shift containing fee pressure—80% payout committed.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morningstar.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. Could you elaborate on the performance of the AlphaCore Equity Fund?

Elena Vasquez: Hi Lisa. AlphaCore blended quant and fundamental for 14.2% Q3 returns, +420 bps over S&P net fees—11 quarters running. Drove $4.2 billion inflows, 15 bps large-cap growth share amid AI rally. Our AI Alpha Engine enhanced this, improving forecasts 15%.

Lisa Chen: And how is the new product Apex AI Innovators ETF performing relative to expectations?

David Chen: Exceeding, Lisa—$900 million AUM since launch, tapping semis hype like ARK peers. Part of our ETF push to $320 billion, +28% YoY. Early retail traction via Schwab/Fidelity, 15% of Q3 flows.

Operator: Thank you. There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Johnathan for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you for joining us today. We appreciate your interest in Apex Global Asset Management. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
